title: Hosted-to-Private Migration Assistant — Release Notes v1.0
author: Aisha Kumar
content:
Summary
-------
This document records the v1.0 release of the Hosted-to-Private Migration Assistant (Migration Assistant). The Migration Assistant is a product-side, self-service tool that automates and guides migration of customer workloads from Redwood hosted inference to a Redwood Private deployment (VPC or on-prem bundle). This release targets enterprise customers with predictable traffic patterns and a first-class path for security review and compliance.

Key highlights (v1.0)
--------------------
- Dry-run simulation engine that predicts cost and latency changes for a representative workload.
- Traffic replay service for staged validation using customer-provided traces (anonymized).
- Configuration translator: converts hosted inference route configs into Private manifest drafts (YAML).
- Rollout orchestration with canary, gradual ramp, and automated fallback to hosted endpoints.
- CLI and web console flows with built-in preflight checks and an audit-ready migration log.
- Integrations: KMS key registration guide, private network validation checks, and IAM role templates.

Why this matters
-----------------
Customers frequently request a low-risk, observable way to move to Private deployments for compliance or data residency reasons. Previously migrations required significant manual work across networking, model pinning, cost-model validation, and on-prem packaging. The Migration Assistant reduces friction by codifying best-practice migration steps and automating error-prone conversions.

Audience and scope
-------------------
- Primary audience: Customer Platform Engineers and SREs working with Redwood enterprise accounts.
- Secondary audience: Solutions Engineers and Account Leads supporting migrations.
- Scope: Inference routes serving token-based text generation, chat, and embedding endpoints. Does not bundle on-prem hardware provisioning (that remains a separate engagement).

Compatibility and prerequisites
-------------------------------
- Supported models: Redwood-verified open models and customer-provided containerized models where the same model artifacts are available to the private runtime.
- Minimum Redwood Console version: 2028-05-01.
- Required customer inputs: sample traffic (1M tokens or representative subset), route config JSON, target network CIDR, KMS metadata.
- Network prerequisites: VPN or Direct Connect configured; egress rules validated for model and telemetry endpoints.

SLOs and success criteria for migrations
----------------------------------------
- Validation pass rate >= 95% for preflight checks.
- Simulation drift: predicted latency within +/- 15% of observed on first canary.
- Rollout success: >= 99% of requests served from Private after ramp, or automatic fallback completes within configured timeout.

What’s included in this release
-------------------------------
1) CLI: redwood-migrate v1.0
   - Commands: init, simulate, translate, dry-run, canary, promote, rollback
   - Example: redwood-migrate simulate --route-id r-1234 --trace-file sample-trace.json --output report.json
2) Console workflows
   - Migration workspace with step-by-step wizard and visual diff of translated config
3) APIs
   - POST /migrations (create)
   - GET /migrations/{id}/status
   - POST /migrations/{id}/actions (canary, promote, rollback)
4) Artifacts
   - Generated migration manifest (YAML) and an accompanying audit bundle (ZIP) that contains simulation reports, CLI outputs, and preflight logs.

Preflight checks (run automatically)
----------------------------------
1. Model compatibility: runtime-level compatibility check for model ops and quantization profile.
2. KV and prefix cache expectations: validates whether cache warmup is needed and estimates warmup tokens.
3. Network connectivity: port and routing checks against supplied CIDRs.
4. Secret bindings: KMS availability and role binding tests.
5. Consumption policy mapping: maps hosted quotas and token bundles to Private capacity estimates.

Migration manifest example (YAML excerpt)
----------------------------------------
```yaml
migration: 
  route_id: r-1234
  target: private-vpc-az1
  model_pin: open-7b-quant-v2
  traffic_split:
    - canary: 5%
    - ramp: [5, 25, 50, 100]
  preflight_checks: [model_compatibility, network_connectivity, kms_bindings]
  rollback_policy:
    on_error: fallback-hosted
    timeout_minutes: 20
```

Runbook: recommended migration flow
-----------------------------------
1. Kickoff and scoping (Solutions Eng + Customer)
   - Confirm objectives, rollback SLA, and audit requirements.
2. Prepare inputs
   - Customer supplies route config, sample trace, and network/KMS metadata.
3. Simulate (local + cloud)
   - Run redwood-migrate simulate and review the generated cost/latency report.
4. Translate and review manifest
   - Use the console diff to validate translated resources and secret mappings.
5. Dry-run (no traffic)
   - Deploy artifacts to private test environment and run internal smoke checks.
6. Canary (live)
   - Start with configured canary percent; measure telemetry for 2x SLO window.
7. Promote or rollback
   - Promote after stability checks pass; otherwise trigger automated rollback.
8. Post-migration audit
   - Generate the migration bundle and upload to customer compliance repo.

Operational commands and examples
--------------------------------
- Start a canary: redwood-migrate canary --migration-id m-20280612-01 --percent 5
- Promote: redwood-migrate promote --migration-id m-20280612-01
- Force rollback: redwood-migrate rollback --migration-id m-20280612-01 --reason "latency spike"

Known issues and limitations (v1.0)
----------------------------------
- Edge case: models using custom CUDA kernels that are not present in the Private runtime will fail model_compatibility check. Manual kernel packaging is required.
- Trace fidelity: highly bursty production traces require sampling; simulation accuracy degrades for highly tail-heavy workloads.
- RBAC: migration actions require admin-level role in both hosted account and private control plane. Documented workarounds exist in the operations guide.

Security and compliance notes
-----------------------------
- All uploaded traces are anonymized client-side by the CLI before upload (PII redaction defaults enabled).
- Migration audit bundles are signed with Redwood KMS and retained for 365 days by default; retention settings configurable per customer.
- KMS integration requires the customer to provide a key ARN (AWS) or equivalent metadata for on-prem HSM registration.

Telemetry and observability
--------------------------
The Migration Assistant emits the following telemetry namespaces: migration.events, migration.simulation, migration.rollout. Default retention for migration traces is 90 days. Built-in dashboards: Migration Overview, Canary Health, Simulation vs. Observed Delta.

Rollout and deprecation plan
----------------------------
- v1.0 rollout: gradual launch to enterprise beta cohort (June 2028), followed by general availability (GA) on 2028-07-15.
- Deprecations: none planned for v1.x. Breaking changes will follow a 60-day deprecation notice.

Support and escalation path
---------------------------
- First line: Solutions Engineering (SE) assigned to the account.
- Second line: Private Deployments Engineering oncall (eng-private-deployments).
- Escalation: open a ticket with priority P0 when rollback fails to complete within configured timeout. Include migration-id and audit bundle.
